alle.ide: A dark green ø180 ball of 6 + 6 crossing mirror-acrylic discs hangs in a thin half-yoke on a stem and round base; the lattice is turned so one family stands square to the tilt axis, which makes the two outermost discs flat ø90 cheeks with an ø8 hole in the centre where the brass pivots go through. The one action is tipping the ball (hole up and back = stemning on the wall, nodded 75 degrees down and forward = arbeid on the table), and the larger right-hand brass pivot is the dimmer knob.
alle.tal: Both poses ALT OK, all seven hard rules green, 16 of 16 checks. 12 plates, 24 joints (0 tenons, 0 rejected, 0 loose), 2 sheets 600 x 400, 10.17 m of cut (10.18 in the arbeid pose), 0.408 kg cut body weighed as 3 mm acrylic, smallest material at a joint 18.7 mm. Cut body 177 x 178 x 179 mm. With the drawn stand: overall height 327 mm, sphere centre 237 mm above the table, base ø150 = 177 cm2 (F9 limit 200), 218 mm wide across the pivots. Pivot holes ø8 are in the cut files of plates 1 and 6 and were read back on the tilt axis (ø7.88, centre x = -78.0 and 78.0).
alle.material: Sphere: 3 mm mirror acrylic, mirror face toward the centre on all 12 plates (6 with speglSide 1, 6 with -1 in scene.json), the back painted matt dark green #2f3d35; cut edges are left as pale acrylic. Stand as drawn: matt dark green powder-coated metal, base ø150 x 10, stem and yoke ø8, yoke 7 mm outside the sphere. Brass: left pivot ø12 and right pivot with a ø22 x 13 dimmer knob. Light module: a plug in the ø37 socket at the pole opposite the hole, with a flush dark green cap. Intended, not modelled: flat battery pack under a lid in the base, wire through stem, yoke and a hollow pivot.
alle.uloyst: Only drawn in the picture: base, stem, yoke, brass pivots, knob, module plug and the bulb stand-in; none of these are engineered, cut or weighed. The 0.408 kg is the acrylic body only, so the total against F8 (1.2 kg) is not checked, nor is tipping (T2). F1 is not shown: mirror faces can reflect the source toward the eye, and the lit tile shows bright mirror strips in the mouth at 75 degrees; nothing measures it and no diffuser round the source is modelled. The pictures show where light goes (ray counts), not lux, so F3 and F6 are not verified. The half-lap joints are slip fits and each cheek is held by only 2 of them; the lattice would need solvent bonding to hang from the pivots, and the cheek's strength was not calculated. How the boss clamps (stud and nut through the ø8 hole), the dimmer, the wiring through the pivot, the battery lid and the module removal (B1) are design intent only. No power cord is drawn. The painted back on mirror acrylic and the visible pale edges were not tested. Only --rask runs: no production files, no STEP, nothing cut. Final full sheet read for the arbeid pose; for stemning the full sheet was read one iteration earlier and the final helt and lys tiles in the pair image.

alle.ide: The quieter, taller sibling: a grey-beige ø200 ball of 8 + 8 thinner (2 mm) mirror discs on a 175 mm stem, with a larger mouth (ø132) and the same square-to-the-axis lattice and ø109 cheeks, but the pivots are small body-coloured bosses. The only brass is a ø32 crown on the light module at the pole opposite the hole: you take it and swing the ball over (hole up and back = stemning, 70 degrees down and forward = arbeid), turn it to dim, pull it to take the module out.
alle.tal: Both poses ALT OK, all seven hard rules green, 16 of 16 checks. 16 plates, 52 joints (0 tenons, 0 rejected, 0 loose), 2 sheets 600 x 400, 18.17 m of cut (18.16 in the arbeid pose), 0.441 kg cut body weighed as 2 mm acrylic, smallest material at a joint 5.0 mm. Cut body 198 x 198 x 200 mm. With the drawn stand: overall height 392 mm in stemning and 400 mm in arbeid (the crown is then on top), sphere centre 292 mm above the table, base ø158 = 196 cm2 (F9 limit 200), 226 mm wide across the pivots. Pivot holes ø8 are in the cut files of plates 1 and 8 and were read back on the tilt axis (ø7.89, centre x = -84.0 and 84.0).
alle.material: Sphere: 2 mm mirror acrylic, mirror face toward the centre on all 16 plates (8 with speglSide 1, 8 with -1 in scene.json), the back painted matt grey-beige #b5ad9f; cut edges left as pale acrylic. Stand as drawn: matt grey-beige powder-coated metal, base ø158 x 10, stem and yoke ø8, yoke 7 mm outside the sphere, pivot bosses ø12 in body colour. Brass: one crown ø32 x 12 on the light module in the ø36 socket at the pole. Intended, not modelled: flat battery pack under a lid in the base, wire through stem, yoke and a hollow pivot.
alle.uloyst: Only drawn in the picture: base, stem, yoke, pivot bosses, brass crown, module plug and the bulb stand-in; none are engineered, cut or weighed. The 0.441 kg is the acrylic body only; total mass (F8) and tipping (T2) are not checked, and a ø200 ball 292 mm up on a ø158 base looks top-heavy, so the base needs the battery and ballast. F1 is not shown: the arbeid lit tile shows bright mirror strips inside the mouth and a lit arc on the yoke from the camera 20 degrees above; nothing measures glare and no diffuser is modelled. Ray counts, not lux: F3 and F6 not verified. The crown passes the yoke only one way round (over the top), so the swing between the poses is about 150 degrees; time (F2) and friction in the pivots are not tested. 2 mm mirror acrylic with 2.15 mm slots and 5.0 mm material at the weakest joint passes the engine's rule, but its stiffness and whether the lattice holds the pivots was not calculated; slip-fit joints would need bonding. Dimmer in the crown, wiring through the pivot, battery lid and module removal (B1) are design intent only. No power cord drawn. Only --rask runs: no production files, no STEP, nothing cut. Final full sheet read for the arbeid pose; for stemning the full sheet was read one iteration earlier (base ø155 x 12) and the final helt and lys tiles in the pair image.

alle.namn: Rist (drum ø162 x 62 mm, 450 mm high)
alle.ide: A plain matt dark-green drum on a thin stem hides a square egg-crate of mirror blades under a flat LED module and opal disc; you only see the mirror grid when you look into the mouth. The one action is tilting the drum on its brass side pivot: mouth down is work light on the table, rolled 130 degrees so the mouth points up and back is mood light on the wall.
alle.tal: From ut/rapport.txt, same in both poses: 10 plan, 10 plates, 21 joints (0 tenons, 0 rejected, 0 loose), 1 sheet 600 x 400, 0.162 kg cut body (engine weighs 3 mm acrylic), smallest material at a joint 18.0 mm, all 7 hard rules ok, 11 of 11 built-in checks ok. Cut length 4.84 m (arbeid) / 4.86 m (stemning). Cut body 158 x 158 x 36 mm. Louvre: 5 x 5 blades, pitch 28 mm, clear cell 25 mm, blade depth 36 mm, so cut-off from the lamp axis is atan(25/36) = 35 degrees across a cell and 45 degrees along the cell diagonal; chosen so the diagonal still stays at 45. Overall, measured from scene.json: 450 mm high in arbeid, about 495 mm in stemning, 244 mm wide, 162 mm deep. Footprint: base ø140 = 154 cm2 (the head hangs outside the base to one side).
alle.material: Lattice: 3 mm mirror acrylic, rendered with mirror on BOTH faces (speglSide 0). Drawn only, as stand-ins: drum housing (lid plus full skirt), ø8 stem and ø140 x 10 base in one matt dark green #2f3d35 (meant as powder-coated steel or aluminium); 3 mm opal acrylic disc ø156 on top of the lattice; brass pivot ø12 and brass knob ø24; cord.
alle.uloyst: Only the 10 lattice plates come from the engine. Housing, opal disc, LED module, stem, base, pivot and cord are picture stand-ins with no joints: how the lattice is held in the drum, the pivot friction, cable route, battery and B1 access are unsolved. Physics caveat: flat vertical mirror blades keep a ray's angle to the axis, so beyond the 35/45 degree cut-off the eye cannot see the opal directly but can see its reflection in the blades; F1 is therefore not shown, and a real specular louvre would need wedge-shaped or satin blades. Both-face mirror needs double-sided mirror acrylic (ordinary 3 mm mirror acrylic has one mirror face). The light source in the pictures is 3 point sources at the opal plane in three cells, not a lit disc; no lux, F3 and F6 not measured. The soft halo above the lid in the lys tiles is the renderer's source sprite, not leaking light. Total weight (F8) and tipping (T2) not computed: the head centre sits 93 mm from the stem, 23 mm outside the base edge. Cameras are non-default in the helt tiles: arbeid is taken from 8 degrees below, stemning from behind (az 150), so the grid shows; from the user's side in stemning you see only the back of the drum. Only --rask was run: no production files, no STEP, nothing cut.

alle.ide: A shallow lens of slats leaning 40 degrees hangs under a thin grey-beige lid; the slats are single-sided mirror with the mirror on the face turned away from the user, so they throw the light forward onto the desk and the eye meets only matt backs. The one action is flipping the head over the brass hinge on top of the stem like turning a page: face down in front of the stem is work light, face up behind the stem the same slats throw the light up and back onto the wall.
alle.tal: From ut/rapport.txt, same in both poses: 10 plan, 10 plates (6 slats + 4 fins), 24 joints (0 tenons, 0 rejected, 0 loose), 1 sheet 600 x 400, 6.41 m cut, 0.243 kg cut body (3 mm acrylic), smallest material at a joint 19.6 mm, all 7 hard rules ok, 11 of 11 built-in checks ok. Cut body 188 x 186 x 48 mm. Louvre: slats at 24 mm pitch leaning 40 degrees, clear gap 20 mm, depth 46 mm at the centre and 22 mm at the rim. Worked out by hand, not measured: direct light leaves between 22 and 52 degrees from the axis on the throw side at the centre (minus 4 to 60 degrees at the rim), nothing direct toward the other side at the centre. Fins at 26 mm pitch, clear 23 mm: atan(23/46) = 27 degrees sideways at the centre, 46 at the rim. Slats and fins still cross at 90 degrees (slot 3.15 mm). Overall, from scene.json: 446 mm high in both poses, 194 mm wide, 280 mm deep. Footprint: base ø150 = 177 cm2 (the head hangs 205 mm in front of or behind the stem).
alle.material: Slats: 3 mm single-sided mirror acrylic, mirror on the down-and-back face in arbeid (speglSide 1, checked in scene.json in both poses), other face matt grey-beige #b9b2a5. Fins: mirror on the face toward the centre, matt outside. Drawn only: lid with a short skirt (ø194 x 25), ø8 stem, ø150 x 10 base in matt grey-beige (meant as powder-coated metal); 3 mm opal acrylic disc; brass hinge barrel ø14 x 36; cord.
alle.uloyst: Only the 10 lattice plates come from the engine. Lid, opal disc, LED module, stem, base, hinge and cord are picture stand-ins: the hinge with stops at 0 and 180 degrees, power through the hinge, battery and B1 access are unsolved. The lens is thin at the rim, so the cut-off is weakest there (60 degrees) and the outer segments in front of and behind the last slat are open. The beam angles are hand calculations; the pictures show where light lands, not lux, and F1, F3, F6 are not measured. In stemning the mirror faces turn toward the user's side and upward; by reflection geometry they should show the ceiling and not the source, but that was not checked in a render. The light source is 3 point sources at the opal plane; the halo above the lid in the arbeid lys tile is the renderer's source sprite. The lys tiles use a camera pulled back (vid 2.1, el 9) and a wall 60 mm behind the rearmost point so the wall wash fits in the frame; at 20 and 35 degree slats it landed above the frame. Total weight (F8) and tipping (T2) not computed: the head centre is 108 mm from the stem, 33 mm outside the base edge. Slots along a 40 degree slant are untested on a laser. Only --rask was run: no production files, no STEP, nothing cut.

alle.ide: A half-sphere shell of crossing plates, matt grey-beige outside and mirror toward the inside, turns like an eyelid around a fixed opal ball carried on a horizontal axle from a one-sided L-shaped line. One turn of the brass knob: shell opening up and back shows the ball to the wall (stemning), shell turned over the ball with the opening down puts the light on the table (arbeid).
alle.tal: Hard rules all green in both poses (grip, delar, orden, klem, gods, plate, snittspor), krav 16 of 16 in both. 12 plates (6 + 6), 24 joints, 0 tenons, 0 loose, 1 sheet 600 x 400 (48-49 % used), cut length 8.34-8.35 m, smallest gods 18.4 mm, cut body 0.341 kg weighed as 3 mm acrylic. Overall height 350 mm with the stand as drawn, ball centre 260 mm above the table, shell ø180, opal ball ø68, width arm to knob 206 mm, foot ø150 = 177 cm2. The two ø8 axle holes (plates 1 and 6) are cut by the engine and read back as ø7.88 on the turning axis.
alle.material: Shell: 3 mm mirror acrylic, mirror face toward the axis, outer face matt grey-beige #b7ad9c (bag material akryl, klaring 0.15, snitt 0.2). Drawn only: opal ball ø68 (opal glass or opal acrylic), ø8 tube line and ø150 x 10 foot in the same matt colour (powder-coated steel or aluminium), one brass knob ø22 on the axle end.
alle.uloyst: Only the 12 plates and their two axle holes are engine geometry; the stand, axle, brass knob, opal ball (drawn as a ø68 bulb stand-in) and the crown plug exist only in the picture. Not solved: how the ball is fixed on the axle and how the axle passes it, the friction that holds a pose, where battery, driver and USB-C sit, how the owner swaps battery and light module (B1). Not checked: lux on the table or wall, glare (F1) - in arbeid the ball's lowest 10 mm hangs below the shell rim and the rim is 236 mm above the table, so a low eye sees it, and a mirror lining can show the ball by reflection; tipping with the foot centred 51 mm off the head; total weight (only the cut body is weighed, and as plain acrylic). The inward mirror faces were not inspected close up. Only --rask was run: no production files, no STEP, nothing cut. Its action is a turn about a horizontal axis, so it is a relative of Globus even though the support is one-sided and the light source stays still.

alle.ide: A cone of crossing plates, matt dark green outside and mirror inside, with the light module and a brass cap in its narrow end, rests loose in a ø100 ring on a thin stem. Lift it, turn it over and drop it back: mouth up it sits in the ring like a funnel and sends the light upward (stemning), mouth down it sits over the ring like a shade and pours the light on the table (arbeid); there is no hinge.
alle.tal: Hard rules all green in both poses, krav 12 of 12 in both. 8 plates (4 + 4), 16 joints, 0 tenons, 0 loose, 1 sheet 600 x 400 (39 % used), cut length 6.06 m, smallest gods 19.4 mm, cut body 0.203 kg weighed as 3 mm acrylic. Cone ø180 at the mouth, ø64 at the crown, 140 mm tall. Ring ø100, 265 mm above the table. Stemning: overall height 371 mm, head from 220 to 371 mm, the ring meets the cone 106 mm from the mouth. Arbeid: overall height 392 mm, mouth 241 mm above the table, the ring sits 24 mm inside the mouth. Foot ø150 = 177 cm2.
alle.material: Cone: 3 mm mirror acrylic, mirror face toward the axis, outer face matt dark green #2f3d35 (bag material akryl, klaring 0.15, snitt 0.2). Drawn only: ø8 stem, ø100 ring and ø150 x 10 foot in the same matt green (powder-coated steel), brass cap ø33 on the crown as accent and control, an opal acrylic sleeve ø40 x 56 round the light source.
alle.uloyst: Weaker than Blunk as a product picture: the 6 x 6 lattice failed the hard rule klem in four tries (outer/middle plates at 70/44, 66/41, 78/46.8, 71/52), so this is a sparse 4 x 4 lattice; the rim is ragged, it reads more as a tulip than a clean cone, and from the side you can see in between the plates. Only the 8 plates are engine geometry; ring, stem, foot, brass cap, module and opal sleeve exist only in the picture. The two seat positions are computed from the nominal cone and never tested: mouth up the ring touches only the edges of the four inner plates, with 34 mm of cone plus the cap below the ring, and nothing checks that it sits steady or cannot be knocked out. In arbeid the stem rises inside the mouth and shadows the table. Not checked: lux, glare (F1) - the opal sleeve is drawn but casts no shadow in the lit view, and the mirror faces can show the source by reflection; light on the wall in stemning is mostly upward, not aimed; tipping; total weight; battery, charging and module swap (B1). Only --rask was run: no production files, no STEP, nothing cut.

rangering.grunn: Form: the calmest of the four lattice bodies and the only one that reads as a ball before it reads as plates. 8 + 8 discs give a fine, even rhythm, and on grey-beige the pale cut edges almost vanish, so 'one matt colour' holds. Base disc, thin line, half-yoke and ball are clear additive forms, and the single brass crown is both accent and handle (rule 5). In the stemning tile the crown sits low on the front like a plug; in arbeid it tops the ball like a bauble cap. Action: visible in the lit tiles. Stemning puts a broad glow on the wall and only two small patches on the table; arbeid lights the table and leaves two patches high on the wall. Brief: weakest here. The arbeid lit tile shows a row of bright mirror strips in the mouth and a brightly lit yoke arc right under it, so 'source hidden' is not what the picture shows. The source is a bare stand-in inside a mirror ball (rule 3), and the yoke throws a shadow line across the base. It is 392 to 400 mm tall on a ø158 base (196 of 200 cm2), with 2 mm plates and 5.0 mm at the weakest joint, 16 plates and 52 joints. The visible body is painted acrylic, which section 7 excludes as main material. Honesty: good. The text names the glare, the top-heaviness and the 150 degree swing, and the report numbers I re-read match (16 plates, 52 joints, 18.16 and 18.17 m, 0.441 kg, 5.0 mm).
rangering.fiks: Put an opal body round the source (the fixed opal ball from Blunk, sized with the brief's luminance formula), so the mirror lining repeats a soft glowing ball instead of a bare point. The bright strips in the arbeid mouth are images of that bare point. Not run.

rangering.grunn: Form: the best new idea. In arbeid it is a plain dome on a single offset line, the most homely silhouette of the six, and the most compact lattice design (350 mm, one sheet). The front and side elevations on the contact sheet are cleaner than the pair tiles. But 6 + 6 plates at 3 mm are coarse: wide see-through gaps and a toothed rim, so next to Måne it reads half as a kit. Action: the clearest difference among the lattice designs. Stemning washes the wall broadly; arbeid gives the widest and smoothest pool on the table of all six. The name explains the action (rule 6), with one brass knob (rule 5) and a one-sided line (rule 2). Brief: the strongest concept on rule 3 and on robustness, because the light source is a fixed opal ball and the shell is a passive shade, so nothing electrical turns. Problems seen: in the stemning lit tile bright mirror patches show through the gaps toward the camera and a grid of light leaks onto the table; in arbeid a bright sliver shows at the rim, and by the author's numbers the ball hangs 10 mm below it. By the brief's own formula (luminance = flux / (pi x area)), a ø68 ball (145 cm2) at 300 lm is about 6 600 cd/m2, over twice the F1 limit of 3 000; about ø100 is needed. That is my hand arithmetic, not a measurement. Honesty: the text is frank, but the pair image does not show the idea. The opal ball is not visible in any of the four tiles beyond a sliver between plates; it is visible in the front and top elevations of the fri/bs and fri/ba contact sheets. A ring-shaped ghost on the wall in the arbeid lit tile is unexplained.
rangering.fiks: Give the shell Måne's density (8 + 8 thinner plates): smaller teeth at the rim, narrower see-through gaps, fewer glints and leaks. This needs a new engine run and is not certain to pass, since the 6 x 6 cone failed 'klem'.

rangering.grunn: Form: the only one that reads at once as a finished Northern product: base disc, thin line, drum, one matt dark green and one brass pivot, which I count as five of the six form rules. It is also the only one where the acrylic is truly inside and the visible body is meant as coated metal, as section 7 asks. But it is an anonymous drum spot: the action is the ordinary tilt of any spot lamp (rule 6 is weak), and the lattice the owner liked is hidden. Action: the cleanest lit pair of the six. Stemning is one soft glow on the wall with a dark table; arbeid is a pool round the base plus a lit band low on the wall. The pool is centred on the lamp's own base, not in front of it, and carries a check pattern from the three point sources. Brief: the source sits behind opal and louvre, the best of the six on 'never naked'. Against that, flat mirror blades do not cut glare (the author's own caveat), the blades need double-sided mirror acrylic, it is the tallest (450 to 495 mm), and the head hangs outside the ø140 base. Honesty: the text is honest, the picture less so. The stemning daylight tile is shot from the wall side and the arbeid one from 8 degrees below, the only views where the grid shows. From the chair in stemning you see the back of a plain drum (front and side elevations of raster/rs). In arbeid the mouth plane is at about 39 cm (450 minus the 62 mm drum, my arithmetic), so the grid is seen only from below that. The grid renders pale grey, not as mirror.
rangering.fiks: Swap the upright two-sided mirror grid for Blad's leaning single-sided slats inside this closed drum, mirror face away from the user and matt back toward the eye. That answers the glare caveat with ordinary one-sided mirror acrylic and throws the work pool in front of the base instead of round it. Not run, and Blad's own lit tiles are too dark to prove it.

rangering.grunn: Form: the same idea as Måne, coarser and busier. 6 + 6 plates with mint-pale cut edges on dark green turn the ball into stripes, the mouth edge is ragged, and it reads as a laser-cut kit more than a calm body. Rule 4 (one matt colour) is visibly broken by the edges, and there are two brass parts (pivot and knob) instead of one. Action: weaker separation than Måne, because both lit tiles spray light everywhere. Stemning lights the wall but also patches on the table, and bright glints show through the gaps toward the camera. Arbeid gives a spiky starburst on the table, patches on the wall and a shadow line from the yoke across the base, which is not the even field F3 asks for. Brief: compact (327 mm, 177 cm2) with sturdy plates (18.7 mm at the weakest joint), but a bare source in a mirror ball and bright strips in the mouth, as the text admits. The visible body is painted acrylic. Honesty: one mismatch. The module cap is described as flush; in the stemning tile it is drawn as a dark cylinder standing out of the ball. The report numbers match (12 plates, 24 joints, 10.17 and 10.18 m, 0.408 kg).
rangering.fiks: Make the cut edges the body colour (painted, or cut from dark-tinted mirror acrylic), so the ball is one dark matt form with shadow gaps instead of twelve striped plates. If only one globe goes forward it should be Måne; Perle then survives as its dark green colourway.

rangering.grunn: Form: the arbeid daylight tile is good: a thin lid with a ribbed lens under it on a line, calm and light. The stemning daylight tile is not: the lens faces up and the slats stand out of the dish as saw-teeth. The page-turn over a brass hinge is the best-named action of the six (rule 6). Action: not shown. Both lit tiles are close to black: stemning is a faint plume high on the wall, arbeid a dim patch in front of the base. They also use a pulled-back camera and a wall moved to 60 mm behind the head, and the renderer sets exposure from the room, so they cannot be compared with the other five. Brief: by the author's numbers the head hangs 205 mm out from a ø150 base at 446 mm, the worst tipping case of the six, and the lens rim is open and thin (22 mm). The beam angles are hand calculations and no picture confirms them. Whether the mirror faces show ceiling rather than source in stemning was not checked. Honesty: the text says all of this, but the picture cannot carry the claim 'throws the light forward onto the desk' beyond the direction of one dim patch.
rangering.fiks: Build the leaning slats as a constant-depth louvre behind a full skirt (Rist's drum), then render the lit tiles with the standard camera and wall. As shown the rim is open, the slats are exposed in stemning, and the light cannot be judged.

rangering.grunn: Form: a kit. Eight plates do not make a cone: the rim is ragged, you see through it from the side, and it reads as a shuttlecock with the mouth up and a card tent with the mouth down. The author says the same and reports that the 6 x 6 lattice failed 'klem' four times. Action: the idea is the most playful and needs no hinge (lift, turn over, drop back), and the arbeid lit tile does show a clear round pool on the table. But both lit tiles show large blown-out mirror patches facing the camera, hard shadows over wall and table in both poses, and in arbeid the stem stands inside the mouth. Brief: as drawn it fails 'never naked' and F1. The loose seat is computed and never tested, and turning a lit head over probably takes two hands (my judgement, not tested). Honesty: high; the text itself calls it weaker than Blunk.
rangering.fiks: Keep the action and change the body: rest Blunk's half-sphere shell (which passes at 6 + 6) loose in the ring instead of the cone. Bowl up it sits in the ring, dome down it sits over it. Not run.

dom.merknad:
Show Måne first (the ball the owner liked, now calm), then Blunk (the best new idea in the same language), then Rist (the contrast: mirror hidden inside a calm coated body). Hold Perle back as Måne's dark green colourway, and hold Blad and Trakt until they are fixed.

What I checked: I read 00-ramme.md and 04-kravspesifikasjon.md, all six pair images at full size and as enlarged halves, and eight full contact sheets (globus/a1s, globus/b1a, raster/rs, raster/bs, raster/ba, fri/bs, fri/ba, fri/ta). I re-read the verdict lines of all twelve rapport.txt files: every run says ALT OK with 7 of 7 hard rules and all checks green (16/16 Perle and Måne, 11/11 Rist and Blad, 16/16 Blunk, 12/12 Trakt). Plates, joints, cut length, weight and weakest material match the claims. The pair images are the first two tiles of each ark.png and are newer than the runs. I ran no engine runs and did not check scene.json, the hole read-backs or the stand dimensions. The scores are my judgement of the pictures.

No tile is corrupt. These are misleading unless captioned:
1. Rist: the stemning daylight tile is shot from the wall side and the arbeid one from below. From the chair the user sees a plain drum, and the grid does not read as mirror. The glow above the lid in the arbeid lit tile is a renderer sprite (the same in Blad).
2. Blad: the lit tiles use another camera and wall distance and are nearly black. They are not comparable with the rest and do not show a mood light.
3. Blunk: the opal ball, which is the idea, is not visible in the four tiles. A ring-shaped ghost on the wall in the arbeid lit tile is unexplained.
4. Perle: the cap is called flush but is drawn protruding.
5. Perle and Måne: 'source hidden' in arbeid is contradicted by the bright mirror strips in the mouth, and in Måne by the lit yoke arc.
6. The UNDER tile on every contact sheet I opened shows only the underside of the base. It is not in the pair images.

Across all six:
- Mirror toward the inside of an open lattice is not hidden. The mirror faces of the far half look out at the viewer through the gaps, which is what the bright glints in the stemning lit tiles of Perle, Blunk and Trakt are. It needs an opal body round the source and a denser lattice.
- Section 7 says hard plastic is never the visible main material. In Perle, Måne, Blunk and Trakt the visible body is painted acrylic with pale edges. Only Rist keeps the acrylic inside a body meant as coated metal; Blad mostly does. Tell the owner the lattice is acrylic standing in for something else, or argue the exception.
- By their own notes the globes need solvent bonding to hang from the pivots, against the brief's target of zero glue joints (00-ramme section 6).
- The requirement spec marks F1, F2, F3, E2, M1 and B1 to be tried before the concept choice on 18.11. These pictures try none of them. Weight (F8), tipping (T2), lux and glare are unchecked for all six.
- The designs pair up as halves of one design each. Måne has the density and colour; Blunk has the fixed opal ball, the passive shell and the one-sided line. Rist has the closed coated drum; Blad has the leaning one-sided slats and the page-turn. Two merged designs are probably a stronger next step than six separate ones. Neither merge has been run.
